text_excerpt: The complainant, a marginal farmer, borrowed Rs. 1,50,000 from the opposite party moneylender at 5% per month (60% per annum compound interest). The loan agreement was written on blank stamp paper and the farmer was asked to put his thumb impression without reading the contents. On default of a single instalment, the moneylender forcibly occupied the complainant's agricultural land measuring 2.5 acres (Khasra No. 142).

The petitioner's illiterate father was asked to sign what was represented to him as a loan receipt. The document was in fact a registered Sale Deed transferring 3 bighas of ancestral agricultural land to the opposite party for a purported consideration of Rs. 50,000 (actual market value Rs. 18,00,000). The Sub-Registrar failed to verify the identity of the parties.

The workmen were made to sign a bond agreement which stipulated 14-hour daily shifts, unpaid overtime during peak agricultural seasons, and a penalty of Rs. 50,000 for early resignation. The employer also withheld original Aadhar cards and ration cards of workers, making escape practically impossible.

Before performing the surgical procedure, the hospital obtained the patient's signature on a consent form that included a clause releasing the hospital, its doctors, and all staff from any liability arising from medical negligence, post-operative complications, or death. The patient was not explained the nature of this waiver before signing.

The respondent moneylender deducted Rs. 12,000 as 'processing fee' upfront from a loan of Rs. 80,000, handing the borrower only Rs. 68,000. Interest was computed on the full Rs. 80,000 at 36% per annum compound. Three signed blank cheques were taken as security. On default, all three cheques were presented simultaneously, causing criminal proceedings under Section 138 NI Act.
